input:
Write a bash script that splits file paths into parts.

Starting files:
--- /home/eval/data/paths.txt ---
/var/log/nginx/access.log
/home/eval/archive.tar.gz
/etc/hosts
relative/dir/README
/home/eval/.bashrc
/opt/app/v1.2/run.sh
--- end ---

For each path, in order, write one line `DIR|BASE|STEM|EXT` to /home/eval/data/parts.txt:
- DIR: everything before the last `/` (every path here contains a `/`);
- BASE: everything after the last `/`;
- EXT: the text after the last `.` in BASE, or empty when BASE has no `.` other than a leading one (e.g. `.bashrc` has no extension);
- STEM: BASE without `.EXT` (BASE itself when EXT is empty).
Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
Each path is split with parameter expansion:

- `DIR` is everything before the last `/`, via `${p%/*}`.
- `BASE` is everything after it, via `${p##*/}`.
- For the extension, a single leading dot is set aside first. That way `.bashrc` gets no extension, while `archive.tar.gz` gets `gz` and `v1.2` in a directory name is ignored.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
in=/home/eval/data/paths.txt
out=/home/eval/data/parts.txt
: > "$out"
while IFS= read -r p || [[ -n $p ]]; do
  [[ -z $p ]] && continue
  dir=${p%/*}
  base=${p##*/}
  # Ignore a single leading dot when looking for an extension
  rest=$base
  prefix=""
  if [[ $rest == .* ]]; then
    prefix="."
    rest=${rest#.}
  fi
  if [[ $rest == *.* ]]; then
    ext=${rest##*.}
    stem=${base%.*}
  else
    ext=""
    stem=$base
  fi
  printf '%s|%s|%s|%s\n' "$dir" "$base" "$stem" "$ext" >> "$out"
done < "$in"
exit 0
```

Expected output, worked out by hand since the script hasn't been run:
```
/var/log/nginx|access.log|access|log
/home/eval|archive.tar.gz|archive.tar|gz
/etc|hosts|hosts|
relative/dir|README|README|
/home/eval|.bashrc|.bashrc|
/opt/app/v1.2|run.sh|run|sh
```
